flags: Genesis Healthcare, a major customer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. It contributed 7.3% of 2025 consolidated revenues, and the company booked $63.9 million of bad debt expense tied to the bankruptcy in 2025.
The company completed the acquisition of NEXDINE Hospitality for an upfront price of $93.5 million, funded with cash on hand. It is expected to contribute over $150 million in annual revenue.
In its third quarter earnings release the company raised its 2027 revenue growth outlook from mid single-digits to low double-digits.

business_model.claim: HCSG sells outsourced management of housekeeping, laundry, linen, facility maintenance and dietary departments to healthcare and senior-living facilities in the United States. Its customers include nursing homes, retirement complexes, rehabilitation centers, hospitals and campuses, and it serves more than 2,700 facilities.
quotes: We provide management, administrative and operating expertise and services to housekeeping, laundry, linen, facility maintenance and dietary service departments within nursing homes, retirement complexes, rehabilitation centers, hospitals and campuses located throughout the United States.

business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, Environmental Services (EVS) and Dietary. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, EVS contributed about 45.2% of revenue ($638.7 million) and Dietary about 54.8% ($774.5 million).
quotes: We are organized into two reportable segments: housekeeping, laundry, linen and other services (“Environmental Services” or “EVS”) and dietary department services (“Dietary”).

business_model.claim: Revenue comes mainly from full-service agreements. HCSG manages the on-site employees and supplies some supplies, and a limited number of management-only agreements leave payroll with the customer. Contracts can be cancelled by either party on short notice after an initial period.
quotes: Our agreements with customers typically provide for a renewable service term cancellable by either party upon 30 to 90 days’ notice after an initial period of 60 to 120 days.

business_model.claim: Management names new customers and added services for existing customers as the primary revenue drivers. It also seeks to pass cost increases through in service billing.
quotes: We believe the primary revenue drivers of our business are our ability to obtain new customers and to provide additional services to existing customers.

business_model.claim: Third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 3.3% to $479.6 million from $464.3 million. The company attributes the increase to client wins and retention, contractual price increases and pass-through costs.
quotes: The increase in revenues was driven by client wins and retention, contractual price increases and pass-through costs to customers.

business_model.claim: Labor is the largest cost. In 2025, labor costs were about 78.3% of EVS revenue and about 58.8% of Dietary revenue.
quotes: EVS labor costs accounted for approximately 78.3% of EVS revenues in 2025 while Dietary labor costs accounted for approximately 58.8% of Dietary revenues in 2025.

business_model.claim: The company can pass union and minimum-wage increases to customers by contract, but not all wage inflation, so a delay or failure to pass through cost increases would squeeze margins.
quotes: Although we have contractual rights to pass union and minimum wage increases through to our customers, we do not have a contractual right to automatically pass through all wage rate increases resulting from wage rate inflation or local job market adjustments, and we may be delayed in doing so.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and risk factors
business_model.claim: Supplies are the second main cost, and Dietary is much more exposed than EVS. Food supplies were about 30.9% of Dietary revenue in 2025, while housekeeping supplies including linen were about 7.2% of EVS revenue.
quotes: In contrast, food supplies consumed in performing our Dietary services accounted for approximately 30.9% of Dietary revenues.
Housekeeping supplies, including linen products, accounted for approximately 7.2% of EVS revenues in 2025.

business_model.claim: More than half of food and non-food dining supplies came through one distributor, Sysco, in 2025, a supplier concentration that could disrupt operations and cost structure.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025, one distributor distributed more than 50% of our food and non-food dining supplies, and if our relationship, or its business, were to be disrupted, we could experience disruptions to our operations and cost structure.

business_model.claim: Customers are mostly long-term and post-acute care operators that depend on Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement. Customer cash flow therefore drives collections and bad debt, a major swing factor in costs.
quotes: Our customers are concentrated in the healthcare industry and are primarily providers of long-term care.

business_model.claim: Credit losses have been large. Bad debt provisions were $83.1 million in 2025 against $46.8 million in 2024, including $63.9 million tied to the Genesis bankruptcy. Genesis was 7.3% of 2025 revenue.
quotes: On July 9, 2025, Genesis Healthcare, Inc. (“Genesis”) filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the Northern District of Texas.
